title: Coda · two of you
notes: The Other Recordist's coda, and the only scene in the game where the RETURNED column is used for what it was ruled for. The guard has been keeping a place for this for years and calling it superstition. Alan's keyring is the callback: the guard has been complaining about it since the cold open, and it is the first thing Alan says, because it is the only part of the job he can still do.

lines.text: The gate booth. The same bored man, the same book, and a second man standing behind you with no shoes on.
He stands up. In eight hours you have not seen him stand up.
I am going to sit down now.

He sits down on the kerb by the barrier, in the rain, and puts his hands on his knees, and the guard brings the chair out of the booth for him without being asked and neither of them says anything about it.
Your keyring is in the chapel. I am sorry. It has been in the chapel for eleven weeks.
He has complained about that keyring to every contractor who has come through this gate since. It was the only way he had of saying the sentence.
He opens the right column. RETURNED. He writes your name first, because you can still hold the pen.
Then he writes the other name underneath it, from memory, without asking for the spelling, because he has been carrying it for eleven weeks and it was never going to be anybody else's job.
I kept a place for it. I thought that was superstition. It was filing.
Two entries, in a column that has been empty all the way up the page, on the last morning this gate is ever going to be manned.
The machines are booked for six.
They are. And there is nobody in it.
That is the whole of what the three of you have done tonight, and it is worth saying out loud once at a gate before anybody drives anywhere.
